utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Zyrapi, the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence to tell the truth still applies, and Mr. Djurdjic is continuing his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, let's pick up where we left off yesterday. Could you please tell me, where were the training centres that the KLA had in Albania in 1998 when you conducted the training?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was staying in Albania, the training was conducted with small groups. One of the centres was in Qerret between Dures and Kavaja. Another one was in northern Albania close to Kukes. It was an old factory which was used for the training of groups of men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, could you please tell me, In March 1999 who was the commander of the Karadak Operational Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March 1999 the commander of the Karadak Operational Zone was Ahmet Isufi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me what brigades were operating in the area of responsibility of the Karadak Operational Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until March I think there was only one brigade, 171.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And after March?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know after March because I handed over my post, and I don't know after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You handed over the post on the 23rd or the 24th of March, 1999. So --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- so that would be the extent of your knowledge, that's what you told me?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, up until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me how many soldiers the KLA had in this operational zone, Karadak Operational Zone, in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there were very few of them, about 200 or 300, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me who was the commander of the Lap Operational Zone in March 1999 when the NATO attack was launched?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of Llapi Operational Zone was Rrustem Mustafa.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many brigades were there in the area of responsibility of the Lap Operational Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what brigades?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me where was the command post of the 151st Brigade and what was the area of responsibility of this brigade?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 151st and 152nd were in the same area, I'm speaking about that time. They did not have separate areas of responsibility. While the 153rd was somewhere else. I can't remember for the moment where the command was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you remember what area of responsibility the 151st and the 152nd had, because you said that they were together, and what was the area of responsibility of the 153rd?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their area of responsibility started from the Prishtine-Podujeve road on the left side of the road, included the Podujeve villages up to the Bajgora villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And 153rd?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 153rd was on the right side of the Prishtine-Podujeve road, including the villages of the Podujeve municipality, on that side of the road. I don't know how many there were and I don't know where the command was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And it extended all the way down to the administrative border with the rest of Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many fighters did the KLA have in this operational zone in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be exact, but I think there were about 2.000 or 3.000 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, could you please tell me who was the commander of the Salja Operational Zone in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March 1999 commander of the Shala Operative Zone was Rahman Rama.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me, do you know where the command of the Salja Operational Zone was located at that time, in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March 1999 the commander of the Shala Operational Zone was in the village of Oshlan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me what brigades were operating in this area of responsibility, we're talking March 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two brigades in this zone, 141 and 142nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell me as far as the 141st command is concerned, where its command was and what its area of responsibility was, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 141st was located in Cicavica -- the command was located in Cicavica, but I can't remember now the exact name of the village in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And where was the command of the 142nd Brigade and where its area of responsibility was?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 142nd was in Shala of Bajgora, and the command was located in Bajgora.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I forgot to ask you this: Where was the command of the Karadak Operational Zone in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember where it was in March 1999. They would move about a lot, so I can't tell you where they were at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you remember where the command of the Lap Operational Zone was in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now the name of the village where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, now as of March 1999 when the NATO air-strikes began, were there any meetings of the KLA staff with the commanders of the operational zones?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After March 1999, we were not able to have any contacts or to have meetings with the zone commanders as we used to do before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when the -- after the NATO air-strikes began, did you have collegium meetings of the KLA General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the General Staff was spread in different places at the time, and they couldn't meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And during NATO air-strikes were elements of the General Staff in Albania too?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The logistics members were there, the Ministry of Defence members were there, but most of the members of the General Staff were inside Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me who of the KLA General Staff members were in Albania once the NATO air-strikes began?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already said, members of the logistics department, the head of logistics was Xhavit Haliti. Azem Syla was there as well, but he was not staff commander, but he was minister of defence at the time. I was there after April as a member of the Ministry of Defence. In May/June Sylejman Selimi was present there as well. Other members were present as well by the end of May and beginning of June, members of the -- such as Thaqi, members of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Am I right when I say that you passed the decision to establish the brigades in February 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The decision to establish brigades was issued earlier, and it was not issued by me but by the department. The brigades began to be formed in November, December, January, and some of the brigades were not fully established until the end of the war. They were in a process of development up until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, yesterday when I asked you about the Pastrik Operational Zone you told me that 121st through 126th Brigade were operating there; but in this decision of the Pastrik Operational Zone commander where areas of responsibility are designated, I found that there was also a 127th Brigade in the operational zone -- in the Pastrik Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained it yesterday, where the brigades were. There was a decision to form another brigade, the 127th, but it was not formed. So the order was given, but it was not formed as a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That means that the decisions that we have need not have been implemented to the full extent, as is indicated in them?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 127th is a case in point, it was not established as a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, am I right when I say that in the planning of large-scale operations, the political administration of the KLA General Staff also took part in 1999, in March?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not always. On some occasions they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I was referring to large-scale operations. And now I would like to know what operations involved the participation of the political administration in 1999.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period, they took part in the preparation of the Shigjeta Operation, the Arrow Operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's clarify. That's the action to launch an attack from Albania in the Kosare border post area. The attack was launched on the 9th of April, 1999; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it started on the 9th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did the political administration take part in the planning of any other operations?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you now tell me, what operations were planned by the staff, the Supreme Command Staff of the KLA, from the 24th of March, 1999, onwards until the time when you stopped being the Chief of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to the Arrow Operation, there were plans for the protection of the population, the defence of territories where the KLA was operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, am I right in saying that you came over to Metohija from Albania in March 1999, that -- and then took ten days to travel to the area of Drenica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I entered in May 1998, 28th of May, not in March. And the journey continued for ten days until I reached Drenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My mistake. Am I right in saying that you were tasked by the General Staff to train troops of the KLA and to verify the capabilities of the local commanders?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that at the time there were no operational zones?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived in May there were no zones, the only exception being Drenica, and in June the Dukagjini Zone began to be formed and the other zones followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that from May 1998, when you came, until November 1998 that only Mr. Selimi, Mr. Bashota, and Mr. Grabovci of all the members of the General Staff were in Kosovo, sometimes Hashim Thaqi when he was not in Albania, but you always were on the move, and you never were together in one place?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. In addition to Selimi, Bashota, and Grabovci, Jakup Krasniqi was always in Kosova, while the others used to move between Albania and Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that there was no daily communication between members of the General Staff and the local commanders?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. To my recollection, there was no communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that apart from you, no other member of the General Staff of the KLA had any experience of a professional military officer, in 1998 while you were there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true as far as the General Staff is concerned, while in the brigades there were professional soldiers involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I'm referring only to the May-to-November 1998 period, not afterwards. From the moment you came to Kosovo and Metohija until your appointment, that is the period that I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that local unit commanders were men of standing in the villages where those units operated?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that on the 15th of June, 1998, in the Dukadjin valley a decision was taking on mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of a decision as such, but I know that at this time the decision to form the Dukagjini Operational Zone was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's see Exhibit P431.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And before this document is brought on the screen, Mr. Zyrapi, and you saw it the day before yesterday and yesterday, these are minutes from Duskaja, Glodjane, Baranski valley, Lusanska valley, and Drinska valley staffs dated 29th of June, 1998. We see who attended the meeting here, and I meant to work on this document to reach the part I am interested in. On page 1 in the Albanian version, S majl, that's Ramush Haradinaj if I'm correct, says we're dealing with the liberation of the whole country through a general uprising. Do you agree that at the time in that part of Kosovo and Metohija that it went for a general uprising or a liberation of a country through a general uprising?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Before the witness, answers I'm trying to find the general uprising portion in the document if my learned colleague could please assist because the Prosecution can't follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Third paragraph from the beginning of the minutes, Smajl speaking, the last part of that sentence, it is about the liberation of the country through a general insurgency.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This shows that Mr. Ramush Haradinaj pointed out the fact that this is not a war of a group or of an individual but of the whole nation, that the liberation of the country should be carried out through a general insurgency, but it's a not a proclamation for mobilisation, it's not a call for mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can get the interpretation of the witness's answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sorry, can I get the last part of your last answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Interpreter, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that Mr. Ramush Haradinaj pointed out the fact that a war is not a war of an individual or of a group but of a whole nation, that this is a general uprising; however, by saying this he is not proclaiming this situation of general uprising or he's not calling for mobilisation, he's just expressing his opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's take a look at the last paragraph of the minutes. Mr. Major is being referred to. Could you please explain who that was.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Major at the time was Sali Veseli.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I think it's supposed to be at the end of this page, starts in Albanian with a sentence: "Tying the strategic operational axes in Junicko field, Keqe, and other parts of the Dukagjin is a prerequisites for the spread of the war and for supplies to those parts which are not supplied and which would lead to the final liberation of Kosovo." Does this go to the creation of a territory or a zone to be used for the supply of arms for the insurgency that we were talking about?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to these meetings, it is about a zone or area that would facilitate the supply of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's turn the page, please. Let's go to page 2. Below the first bold letters Smajl there's a paragraph attributed to The Major. After that The Major read the order to mobilise the Junicko field dated the 15th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what the document says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There was an order in Junik area on mobilisation on the 15th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to ask you in the penultimate paragraph Mr. Mala is speaking. Could you please explain who that person was.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mala, as far as I remember, was a pseudonym of Alush Agushi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at the third sentence. He says: "What about the misuse of insignia, uniforms, and weapons?" Could you please explain what Mr. Mala is referring to?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but according to this document there were misuse of insignia and uniforms at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go to the last paragraph. Mr. Haradinaj, or Smajl, takes the floor in the first sentence and says: "To assist one another in future we have to supply weapons to the whole population above the age of 16." Did this mean that all the persons above the age of 16 would be taking part in the general insurgency and that they were to be provided with weapons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says 16 years of age, but to what I know it was 18 and older, persons of the age of 18 and older could join the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But Mr. Haradinaj obviously thought that the age 16 was enough for somebody to be recruited and mobilised and able-bodied. Let's continue. Mr. Zyrapi, on the penultimate page, that would be page 4 in the Albanian and 5 in English. Mr. Zyrapi, I would like to quote Mr. Agron. Could you please spell out his name.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Agron is Rexhep Selimi, it's his pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Selimi is saying: "I'm explaining to you that you can be called the Local Operational Staff of the Plain of Dukagjin, while bearing in mind the KLA's division into zones. The whole of Kosovo is one operational zone without ... regions." Could you please comment this.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To what I know from the time I was there, the Kosova area, overall area, was divided into operational zones, but maybe this is an influence from the LPK, the patriotic movement that I mentioned, that regarded Kosova as one zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that local, commanders until autumn 1998, took independent and autonomous decisions on the actions that they would be undertaking?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the area that I know and according to the information I had at the time, yes, that was so in some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that until autumn 1998, General Staff of the KLA did not function in terms of the prevailing military doctrine?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To what I know, yes, it is so more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that on the 18th of June, 1998, there was an attack on a convoy of military and police vehicles at the place called Iglarevo, in the Klina municipality, and that on that occasion a number of persons were suffered, casualties or fatalities?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this incident. I was not there at the time; and as I said, I don't know of this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, when -- where were you on the 18th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was in the territory of the Pashtrik Zone, touring the units of the Pashtrik Operational Zone and assisting them. So I was not in this territory that you mentioned during this time, and I didn't receive information about this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you receive any information that there was a blockade of the Pec-Prizren road and that, from the direction of Pec, barricades were erected at the Dolac village, Klina municipality, and from the direction of Pristina the barricades went up in the municipality of Glogovac in the village of Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blockade of the roads at Llapushnik and at the territory between Kijeve and Kline, I don't remember the exact name of the village, it is true that the roads were blocked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that Kijevo was blockaded for a month and that the KLA forces tried to capture Kijevo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that it was blocked; however, I don't know whether it was captured or not during this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I did not say "captured," but there were attacks with the intent to capture Kijevo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know that the road was blocked, but for these attacks with this intention, I'm not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it known to you that Tahir Zemaj issued an order to block the Pec-Pristina road?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to June 1998? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Am I right in saying that in the Lapusnik village there was a KLA prison in that period, in 1998, summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether at any point in time there was a prison in Lapusnik, and in which period if you do remember?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, no, there wasn't in any period, not in 1998, not in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it known to you that the KLA captured the Obilic thermo-electric plant in 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have information that this happened, that KLA entered an area of Mirash and had it under its control for some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know any information that a bus belonging to the thermo power-plant of Obilic with nine passengers was abducted at roughly the same time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no information about that because I was not in this territory at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that in July 1998 you became chief of the operational administration of the General Staff of the KLA, I think it was on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. In mid-July I was appointed chief of the operational department of the General Staff of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that at the time, in 1998 when you were appointed chief of the operational section of the General Staff of the KLA, that the KLA held 40 to 50 territories in Kosovo and Metohija under their control was centred around Malis [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact percentage, but quite a big part of this territory was under its control, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What I just put to you is -- I don't know if you recall that interview that you gave to the Zeri, that's when you mentioned the percentages. Do you now recall now? Have I jogged your memory?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was interviewed, most probably I did give the percentage, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you, in fact, added that the policy pursued by the Bukoshi's government was better -- had it been better and had the cooperation with the army been better, then greater amount of territory would have been taken; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that the KLA in July 1998 wanted to place another town under its control, another town apart from Malisevo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July at the time, the aim of the KLA was to spread the territory, and when I became head of operations I began to tour the area of responsibility of Dukagjin; however, I was not aware of such intentions to capture a town or another territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, I'm looking for that part of the interview that you gave to the Zeri where you noted that in addition to Malisevo -- well, I don't want to waste our time on that. It's not so important. Thank you. Let's move on. Am I right when I say that in the summer of 1998, it was widely known that the Albanian civilians were killed by the KLA for alleged cooperation or collaboration with Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't know who. I did hear this as an information, but I didn't have any other knowledge, concrete knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And am I right that the General Staff of the KLA informed the public about that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying it didn't, but I wasn't involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I'm not saying that you took part, that this was done under your control, but what about your information and knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only rumours, but not correct, accurate information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that the KLA General Staff and KLA generally never undertook investigations about the murders and killings of Albanian civilians loyal to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, in 1998, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to bring up D002-20-51 paragraph 37, please. That would be page 7 in English, in my version. No indication of page in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see paragraph 37, please?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, that is your statement which you gave on the 25th of November, 2005.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true what is stated in your statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this paragraph 37 as evidence, it's paragraph 37.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At the moment we haven't seen an English text, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. That would be page 7 in English. Yes, page 7, last paragraph on that page. [In English] Yes, I have ... [Interpretation] Your Honour -- well, if there's an error, I can read it. Perhaps it would be a good idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Something, I believe, is happening now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I can tell you that's D000 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We -- the problem is an English version cannot be located in e-court. We will mark for identification paragraph 37 of the statement of the 25th of November, 2005, and perhaps you can take it up with the Registry staff after we have sat today. And when we find an English version of it, it can be admitted as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have the ERN number of -- for the whole of the statement that Mr. Zyrapi gave on the 25th of November, 2005, but let us move on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D00060 MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, in July 1998 were you in the Dukadjin Valley?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in July 1998 I was in the Dukagjin Plain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the KLA General Staff, did it decide to attack Orahovac on the 17th, 18th, and 19th of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know who made this decision to launch an attack on Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I know, I was a member of the staff at the time, I was direct -- head of the operations department, and none of the members of the staff gave that order to attack Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm asking you whether you learned who had issued the order to attack Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just could I ask my learned colleague, I've listened to this line of questioning. So far this witness has not confirmed that even an attack on Orahovac occurred. Could you maybe clarify that first with the witness, so that we see what the basis of the witness's answers are. Suggesting to him that attack orders were filed, don't help us at this point in time if the witness doesn't even recall whether there was an attack on that town in July 1998. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, my learned colleague, but there is an entire statement made by this witness about the knowledge about the attack on Orahovac and his stay in Orahovac. That's why I didn't do it gradually to lay the foundations; and secondly, this is the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Zyrapi, do you know or did you learn at any point who issued the order to attack Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to some inquiries I made at the time, it was the commander of the unit that was in Rahovec organised the attack, but he was killed. It was impossible to confirm that with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many days did the KLA hold Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember how long they held Rahovec because I was not there. On the 18th and 19th of July I returned from Dukagjin, and at that time Rahovec was not under KLA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you meet Mr. Hashim Thaqi near Orahovac at the time when you went there yourself?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I met all the members of the General Staff, including Hashim Thaqi, upon my return.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me where you actually met with Mr. Thaqi?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Mr. Thaqi outside Rahovec. The place is called Rasat e Rahovecit. There I also met the other members of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right that Mr. Thaqi ordered that the road be cut off with a bulldozer?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, do you know how many civilians were killed by the KLA in Orahovac during the time that it was in its hands?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never had that information at my disposal, what you're mentioning now, the number of civilians killed by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know that some civilians were arrested and taken to the prison in Malisevo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When I went there, there were Albanian civilians who were leaving Rahovec and were trying to get shelter in other parts of the country, such as in Suhareke.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know that the KLA had its prison in Malisevo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There wasn't a prison there at that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in July 1998 the KLA attacked the village of Terusa [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that there was an attack in Opterusa, but I was not there, I was outside the territory of the Pashtrik Zone. I was in another zone in the outskirts of Prizren. It's there that I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well -- but isn't Prizren in the Pastrik Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but at that time in June/July, it had not been formed yet. There was no command yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that on the 19th you were close to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when I returned from Dukagjin, I was there on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, how far is the place where you were from Opterusa?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the crow flies, I would say 15 or 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you hear that the KLA attacked and liberated Retimlje on the 17th of July?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about that. At that time I was in the Dukagjini Plain area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And did you hear that the KLA liberated Zociste, that was on the 21st of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The 21st of July there were fightings at that time, not only there but also in Bllace, in the direction of Llapushnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the KLA imposed a tax to finance its activities and that civilians had to pay this tax?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period from the time when you came to Kosovo and Metohija, so May 1998, throughout your stay there.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to have on our screens P00439.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, the date here is the 2nd of July. It's a decision on assignment. Could you please explain to me what -- to what post is Officer Ujku assigned?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see it here in this document, what kind of duty he was being assigned to. He is just being transferred or reassigned, but it does not say anything about the task he was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But this is not a document on the transfer from one post to another; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, from one unit to another, which means reassignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, please listen to me, you can't see that from this document. What is the sense of this document?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the operational zone has issued a document called reassignment, which reassigns the officer, Ujku, from the Dukagjini Operational Zone to the Dujake village, but it does not say what post he is supposed to take there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I'm sorry, but is the village of Dujak outside of the Dukadjin Operational Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in the Dukagjini Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have document P441 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, this is a document that you yourself signed. The date is the 28th of November, 1998, it is sent to the commanders of the operational zones. Now I want to know -- I want you to explain what it says in item 1 of this order. "The operational zone commanders are to increase checks and to involve the members of the command, the military police commanders, to urgently stamp out any negative trends and the abuse of persons and private property." Could you please explain to me what incidents are you talking about here?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order, speaking about negative phenomena, is based on the complaints of zone commanders, about people who had moved from one area to another, had taken property from people without issuing any kind of certificate. This order attempts to do this to increase the control of the zone commanders in order for them to stop this kind of phenomenon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who abused persons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to reports, there were some soldiers from some units doing those kinds of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you explain to me item 3, what kinds of inappropriate behaviour are we talking about, inappropriate behaviour towards civilians?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the same thing on the basis of the complaints or reports I received from the zone commanders, but also from the civilian population, about incorrect or inappropriate behaviour by KLA soldiers towards people and their property; and this order attempts to address exactly that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You issued this order in order to stamp out those kinds of behaviour that you listed in this order; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is in the framework of taking disciplinary measures to stamp out negative phenomena.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have just a few documents to go through with the witness, so perhaps I could do that after the technical break because I think the time has come for it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 4.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Before we bring in the witness, I've been informed that this glitch in the e-court has been eliminated and under D0024953 marks the English translation of the witness's statement taken on the 25th November 2005, and hereby I move for that transcript or that statement to be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thought it was only paragraph 37 that you had tendered. Well, that being so, the document marked for identification as D60 will become Exhibit D60.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to ask the usher to bring up P437, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, this is your order dated 20th January 1999. In paragraph 1 of this order you order to operation zone commanders to compile regular daily combat reports in the morning between 10.00 and 11.00 hours and in the evening between 20 and 2100 hours. What is the purpose of such regular daily combat reports, if you could explain to us, please.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order that was issued and the request that they report was in order to have a clear idea of what was going on in the operational zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that the failure to submit such reports would bring criminal responsibility over the commander of the operational zone in question?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if they did not send in the reports, then they would.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zyrapi, am I right in saying that at the time the Kosovo Verification Mission was in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We've dealt with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please bring up document P442, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I would like you to explain this order by the commander of the Pastrik Operational Zone. Am I right in saying that the military police does not carry out investigating judge's instructions if they do not have an order to do so by the operational zone commander?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order says that if the investigating judge has asked to carry out investigations in the zone, that request is sent to the military police, but the military police needs the approval of the zone commander to execute it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But this does not have anything to do with investigations. So I am right in saying that an operational zone commander has to issue an order to the military police so that the military police can carry out orders of the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which means that a military court investigating judge is not autonomous in his work, particularly in terms of having his orders carried out?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order has been executed, but in order for him to be able to use the military police of that zone, the zone commander needed give that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you are a career officer, and you know that instructions of the military investigating judges are to be carried out, military police organs, and military organisations; am I right in presuming so?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like Mr. Usher to bring up P435 on the screen, please -- page first, please. Thank you. Could we please go to page 2 of this document. Your Honours, I would like a previous explanation. There is a set of decisions in this exhibit, 304, that I received from the OTP. I would like to know whether all documents submitted to me have been tendered into evidence and accepted; and if not all of them, then which of them were because those documents do not have any interconnections. They come from different structures even.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: All of them have become an exhibit, the one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then I will deal with only those that I'm interested in. Please go to page 02460. If I may of assistance, it is an attack order without a date, and it concerns the Pastrik Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To assist, I believe it's the next page, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, could you please tell us, since there is no date on this document, when was this document issued if it's known to you judging by its contents?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this document and the documents we saw earlier are documents used in the training of battalion commanders. They served as a template, as an example, how to train battalion commanders. They are not orders in their full meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this document contain forms or templates that you used for training?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a sample document used in that training, as are the other documents that I have produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But I'm a bit confused because one bears the signature of Ekrem Rexha, and there is a stamp dated the 4th of February, 1999. But thank you. I will accept that these were just templates and had no force. Another question: Where were you between 25th of March, 1999, until 2nd of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th of March, I was at the command in Divjake. On the 26th I went to the commander of the Pashtrik Operational Zone; and I was stationed in the Pashtrik Operational Zone and in the Berisha area, moving around this territory, until April 1999, 2nd April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please remind me where the commander of the Pastrik Operational Zone was at the time, 26th?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 26th I went to his command in Nishor village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, for your patience. I have concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Now, Mr. Neuner, is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Very few, Your Honours, probably I can deal with this in two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you were asked today and yesterday by my learned colleague about combat operations from the KLA. What I'm interested in is: Could you tell us briefly what was the reaction of the civilian population towards combat operations carried out by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can be more specific about the operations. Which operations?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For example, you mentioned Operation Arrow in your evidence. I'm interested, so to speak, whether the civilian population, as the result of Operation Arrow, had to leave certain territories?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Operation Arrow was carried out at the border area between Albania and Kosova; however, the other operations mentioned here carried by the KLA had as their goal the defence of the territories, the evacuation of the population, and finding shelter for the population. So in these type of operations, there was no specific reaction of the population toward us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to be a little bit more specific --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask for interpretation of this witness's answer, please, the one -- the answer to the last question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to say whether you are now getting Serbian interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I understand it. I read it in English. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Carry on, please, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to be a little bit more specific. You said this Operation Arrow was in the border area between Albania and Kosovo. Was through that or as a result of that operation any civilian population moved from a territory?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this operation at this territory there was no population. It had moved earlier from that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know the reason why the population had moved earlier away from that territory?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During even the earlier Serb offensive, the proposition was expelled from the villages and was sent to Albania and other directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you: Do you recall a KLA operation which resulted in the permanent removal of the local population from its own territory? And I'm referring to the period 1998 till 1999.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recall any KLA operation which caused that the population in Kosovo or part thereof had to move across the border into Albania or Macedonia in order to escape the KLA operation?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To what I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, you'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questions for you. The Chamber would like to thank you for your assistance with the answers you've given and for your being prepared to come to The Hague once again. You are now excused, and the court officer will assist you out. Thank you indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. The next Prosecution witness is Mr. Jose-Pablo Baraybar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation that is shown to you on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Now, Ms. Kravetz, you have some questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Could you please start by stating your full name and present occupation for the record.

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: My name is Jose-Pablo Baraybar. Shall I spell that? My first name is J-o-s-e, the second one is P-a-b-l-o, my last name B-a-r-a-y-b-a-r. I am the executive director of the Peruvian Forensic Anthropology Team by its acronym EPAF.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what are you by profession, Mr. Baraybar?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: I'm a forensic anthropologist.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In June 2002 where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: I was the head of the office on missing persons and forensics, by its acronym OMPF, by the United Nations Mission in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when did you cease your employment with OMPF?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: I ceased my employment with the UN as a whole on the 1st of May of 2007.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In 2006, in late October and early November 2006, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Before coming to court today, did you have the opportunity to review this statement?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And having reviewed this statement, are you satisfied that the information contained in the statement is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you also provide an expert report to the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what is the main topic of your report?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: The main topic is examination of forensic inspection of the remains that were found in Serbia proper in three mass graves and were then returned upon identification to Kosovo to the custody of my former office.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness is kindly asked to pause before answering for interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, I note that you don't have your headphones on. Since we're both speaking the same language, you need to wait -- make a pause between question and answer so everything is recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are being translated into a number of other languages as well, and we have to allow time for the process. Gradually you'll get used to the pausing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You were explaining the main topic of your report. Is it correct that your report is attached to your statement as appendix C?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender both the statement and the report, this is 65 ter 02794.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: First the statement will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: It's the same 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00453, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the report ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00454, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, did you also prepare a corrigendum to page 11 of your report, which is a corrigendum to one of the graphs on this page of the report?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender this one page into evidence, it's 02795.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00455, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Appendix A to your statement contains your CV which I don't intend to go through in detail as its self-explanatory, but I would ask you if you can briefly summarise your academic training in the field of forensic anthropology for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Certainly. I have a Bachelor of Arts, a B.A. in archaeology from University of San Marcos in Lima, Peru. I have a Master's of Science at the University of London, combining bio-archaeology, physical anthropology, and forensics. I am currently finishing my doctorate in science at the University of Strasbourg, in France.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. And since you provided your CV to the Office of the Prosecution in October, 2006, have you published any peer review articles in your field?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Yes, I have. Actually, they were published between 2007 and 2008 primarily, including a book co-authored with a colleague of mine, Erin Kimmerle on skeletal trauma within human rights violations and modern warfare; it is a textbook, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you told us that you're currently employed in the Peruvian forensic anthropology institute. What are your current tasks within this organisation?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: I am a member of the Peruvian forensic anthropology team. It's a non-profit organisation who advocates on the use of forensic sciences in the search of the missing during the internal conflict of Peru between 1980 and 2000. I was appointed as executive director based on my qualifications, experience, exposure, I would say. Primarily I advise the team on forensic issues and strategy issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And before testifying in this case, have you previously testified in other cases as an expert witness in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: I have indeed. As a matter of fact, I was also the resident forensic expert of this Tribunal between 1996 and 2002, first in the Rwanda Tribunal and in this Tribunal; and yes, I have testified in a number of cases in this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender appendix A, this is the witness's curriculum vitae, which is attached to his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Um --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Unless it's going to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I had rather assumed it was part of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. If it's going to be entered -- since the report got a different number, I was tendering it separately. That's fine, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The report has a different number because of its separate significance.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Baraybar, before we turn to your report, I want to ask you some questions about your statement. In your statement you describe the procedures and protocols that were in place to repatriate the mortal remains found in clandestine mass graves in Serbia, you speak about three such mass graves, Batajnica, lake Perucac, and Petrovo Selo, to Kosovo. Could you tell us when the first repatriation of mortal remains found at these mass graves from Serbia to Kosovo was organised?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Certainly. In November 2002, we must remember that the office of missing persons and forensics was opened in June 2002. By November 2002 the first repatriation of eight, if I recall well, sets of remains took place from Serbia to Kosovo. These were the remains found at the site of Petrovo Selo under code PS in the report. This was arranged at the time with the forensic institute in Nis, and one of the three protocols you mention, that is the protocol on the repatriation of mortal remains.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I understand from your statement that the exhumations of the mortal remains found at these three sites where the mass graves were discovered were carried out prior to the establishment of OMPF; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, in your statement when you're referring to one of these two protocols, the protocol on exchange of forensic experts and expertise, you refer to the fact that the mortal remains were re-exhumed from the holding facilities where they were in Serbia and that an OMPF was present during these examinations and also to ensure the secure transport to Kosovo. When did this take place that OMPF experts began to attend the re-exhumation of bodies?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: If -- again, I think from my recollection, having been a long time now, this happened in November 2002 with the first eight sets of remains. There was always an OMPF representative present when these activities took place. If I recall well, the Petrovo Selo remains were actually reburied in a cemetery or something of the kind and were still temporary holding facility, but was like a cemetery, they were buried; while the remains from Batajnica, for example, in Belgrade, were kept in some kind of underground tunnel or bunker or something of the kind, close to the Danube; that's what I recall. But in any occasion there was somebody present from my office or former office to oversee the process and accompany the remains back to Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I understand from your statement that these remains were identified as coming from Kosovo based on DNA samples and testing done by the OMPF; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: It is correct. However, the first eight sets of remains did not have at the time DNA results, as such. As a matter of fact, we were able to obtain from the Serb authorities photographs of the clothing of the dead, meaning Petrovo Selo in this case, and organised an exhibition of the photographs of the clothing for family members to identify some of the items of clothing, they were so identified; and based on that, we drew a number of presumptive identifications of these eight people upon discussion with our colleagues in Nis. And based on that, these bodies were returned to Kosovo. All the other remains that came afterwards did come, however, with DNA results.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did the DNA results for these eight set of remains, the first eight set of remains, become available subsequently?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, when you prepared your report and you gave this statement to the OTP, had the repatriation of remains from Serbia to Kosovo been concluded or was it still ongoing?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: No, it had concluded.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when this process was concluded, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: I do not recall exactly. I would say it happened early 2006 most likely, but again it is just based on my recollection. I could not be totally precise on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 29 of your statement you speak about the chain of custody of how these remains were transferred from -- to Serbia and later handed over to OMPF, and you indicate that when they were handed over, OMPF proceeded to give or carry out a forensic inspection. Can you explain what's the purpose of these forensic inspections?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Well, the issue is the following: We at the time were under tremendous pressure, of course, of the families primarily in Kosovo to guarantee in a way that the remains that have actually come from Serbia had or not DNA results were the remains of their loved ones. And based on this, what we needed to do is contrast in a way the inventory we had received with the remains that were contained in the body-bag. Every started as a cursory examination to say there is a body in the bag and reports are referring to one body as well. The problem then became that these inspection or examination became something slightly more complicated when we found some inconsistencies between the contents of the bag and what was stated on the report. To give you an example, we may find the remains of multiple individuals within a bag that allegedly contained the remains of one single person. Obviously, the DNA results spoke about one person and not many people being identified. Therefore, we could not just return the remains as they were to the families. So the forensic inspection became like a second examination, certainly a much more cursory examination, but a second examination that looked at whether we had only one person or more than one; and second, whether there was some kind of coincidence between the description in the autopsy report we received from the Serbian authorities and what actually was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So just so we're clear, when you said it became a bit more complicated because there were inconsistencies between the contents of the bag and what was stated in the report, you were referring to the reports that accompanied each set of remains?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: That is correct. The autopsy report provided by the Serbian authorities from any of the forensic institutes that participated in the examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And who would normally participate in these forensic inspections?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: At OMPF we had multi-disciplinary teams of pathologists, anthropologists, radiographers, scene of crime officers, sometimes even an odontologist that was present during these inspections.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you yourself participate in any of these forensic inspections?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: In quite many of them. I could not really give you a precise number, but in a few dozens of them I was present and actually conducting some of them myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You spoke about there being a pathologist as a member of the team that conducted these forensic inspections. What would be the role of a pathologist during these inspections?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: The pathologist is normally a person who would certify the cause of death, and that is why in the reports that I submitted together with my statement back then, the signature of the -- of the inspection report would be done by a pathologist, the one specifying or certifying that these persons died of this or that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what would be the role of something like yourself, a forensic anthropologist?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Well, you know that when people are killed and time passes, tissues decay, decompose, and sometimes disappear. What is normally left are only bones. Pathologists are medical doctors trained primarily to work with soft tissues, with organs of some kind; and anthropologists are trained to work with bones. In order to determine the most probable cause of death, meaning what is the injury that likely killed a person, an anthropologist, in order to assist the pathologist, must reconstruct as much broken bones as possible. Violent death in general terms is accompanied -- I'm being very general here - with broken bones. So it is some kind of a jig-saw puzzle, if you wish, besides certainly normal other determinations like age, sex, height, handedness, and things of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And were your findings during these forensic inspections recorded in any way?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Certainly. I provided back then a form, a forensic inspection form, per each body that was examined. So every body or body-bag, let's put it that way, that came from Serbia at the time was accompanied by an autopsy protocol from the Serbian authorities; and to this one we attached, after we finished our examination, another short summary form indicating the findings of the forensic inspection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were the standards that were applied during these forensic inspection reports appropriate or accepted standards in international science of -- forensic science?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Most definitely. They were, and they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And was also a death certificate produced at the conclusion of these forensic inspections?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: That is correct. If I may elaborate just for a second, just for the sake of clarification. We received in addition to the autopsy protocol from the Serbian authorities, death certificate reflecting what the Serbian experts have actually found during the examination. We produced a second death certificate based on our forensic inspection. Mind you, there was also obviously a political issue, sensitive issue, to provide, at the time, Albanian families with death certificate that was written in Cyrillic. I mean, it was really politically incorrect at the time to do such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we please have Exhibit 02394 -- this is 65 ter 02394 up on the screen. And I would like page 1 of that exhibit. If we could zoom in on the document a bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the document that is there before us?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Can you explain what this is?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: This is the death certificate that OMPF -- one of which parts was the office of the medical examiner issued, a standard death certificate issued in any type of case. So it could be a so-called historical case, such as the one dealing with missing persons, or it could be a recent case of a recent homicide or traffic accident or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We see that right under the name of the person here identified there is a code which starts with a 2Ba and it says 006. Do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: That is the code that each of the body-bags had. That is the code that was given to the remains exhumed by the Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So if I understand correctly, this code was assigned by Serbian authorities and you maintained the same code in your -- the death certificates that were issued by OMPF?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what would the Ba stand for, 2Ba reference number?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Batajnica, the site of Batajnica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we turn the page, please, next page. And if we could zoom in on the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So we have here that the cause of death is set out as gun-shot to the head, chest, and to the right arm. Would this have been the cause of death that was established during the forensic inspection of these remains?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we go to page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Can you explain what it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could zoom out of the document a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the forensic inspection report that is the summary of findings after the forensic inspection. After we received the body-bag, we opened the body-bag at the mortuary, we laid out the remains, we re-examined them. And as you see, the level of detail is certainly less than a full autopsy, but nevertheless detailed enough as to account, for example, for injuries and these kind of things.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We see here that we only have the code, 2Ba-006, which we saw on the death certificate. You had told us before that you -- that the identities of the victims were established through DNA analysis. So how were you able to know which identity to indicate in the death certificate for these remains?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: In order to minimise any influence by the examiners or the people that were examining the remains, these people were provided only with the codes. I mean, they were provided with a bag for them to actually see whatever was in the bag. They may -- at some point they did have the original autopsy report with them to try to contrast and to go faster. But in some occasions autopsy reports were not even translated, and the people we had did not necessarily read Serb, so they could not really understand. When this inspection was finished with that number the identification unit were the ones elaborating or filling in the information with the pathologist on the death certificate and then they put the name. So we did not have names at the onset of the process. So if somebody - I do not know - could have a special request, for example, by a family member saying, My father or mother or whoever is there, can you please tell me something? They didn't know that. They just had a number. That's why the forensic inspection reports have only numbers, the case number.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, there are a series or sets of forensic inspection reports and death certificates which are referred to in this witness statement. I'm not going to go through the whole batch because they are quite lengthy documents, but I would seek to tender them into evidence at this stage. The one that we were just looking at is 02394. The other ones referred to in this statement are 02454, 00943, 00944, and 02799.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Has P00456, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we now have Exhibit 00213 up on the screen, and if we can display that for the witness both in the English and in the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Can you explain what it is?

utterances.speaker: JOSE-PABLO BARAYBAR
